question:
A 22-year-old female with a history of chronic bipolar disorder presents with amenorrhea for 2 months.
Her menstrual cycles are typically regular, occurring every 30 days. She has recently entered a new
sexual relationship without reliable contraception. Her medical history reveals successful maintenance
therapy with lithium, following failed trials of lamotrigine, quetiapine, and risperidone. A previous
attempt to discontinue lithium resulted in severe depression and a suicide attempt. Her pregnancy test
today is positive. Which of the following is the most appropriate management approach for her bipolar
disorder? Answer Choices: (A) Start psychotherapy alone (B) Switch to valproic acid (C) Switch to
quetiapine with close monitoring (D) Start combination therapy with lithium and lamotrigine (E)
Discontinue lithium immediately (F) Transition to risperidone (G) Continue lithium monotherapy (H)
Supplement the patient with 3–4 mg of folate per day (I) Transition to olanzapine (J) Initiate
electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)
 A. Start combination therapy with lithium and lamotrigine
B. Supplement the patient with 3–4 mg of folate per day
C. Discontinue lithium immediately
D. Initiate electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)
E. Switch to valproic acid

F. Continue lithium monotherapy
G. Switch to quetiapine with close monitoring
H. Transition to risperidone
I. Start psychotherapy alone
J. Transition to olanzapine
